Citrus-Rosemary Popcorn

Served at: Polaris Meteor Watch & UFO Evening

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 10 min

Citrus-Rosemary Popcorn is a zesty and fragrant snack perfect for the Polaris Meteor Watch & UFO Evening, where stargazers gather to enjoy celestial events. This popcorn combines bright citrus notes with earthy rosemary, creating a unique treat that complements the magical night sky experience.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (100 g) popcorn kernels
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil or coconut oil
  • 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • 1 teaspoon orange zest
  • 1/2 teaspoon sea salt, or to taste
  • 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, melted (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon sugar (optional, for slight sweetness)

Method

  1. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat, adding three popcorn kernels to test the temperature.
  2. Once the test kernels pop, add the remaining popcorn kernels and cover the pot with a lid.
  3. Shake the pot occasionally to prevent burning and allow the kernels to pop evenly.
  4. When popping slows to about 2 seconds between pops, remove the pot from heat and transfer the popcorn to a large bowl.
  5. In a small bowl, combine the chopped rosemary, lemon zest, orange zest, sea salt, and sugar if using.
  6. Drizzle the melted butter over the popcorn, then sprinkle the citrus-rosemary mixture evenly over it.
  7. Toss the popcorn gently to distribute the flavors thoroughly.
  8. Serve immediately for the best flavor and crunch.

Tips

  • Use fresh rosemary for the best aroma and flavor; dried rosemary can be too overpowering.
  • For a vegan version, omit the butter or substitute with a plant-based alternative.
  • Experiment with other citrus zests like lime or grapefruit for different flavor profiles.
